hints: Look at both ends of the molecule separately, as $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CHO}$ contains two different functional groups that can be oxidised.
Recall that with excess hot acidified dichromate, a primary alcohol is fully oxidised to a carboxylic acid and an aldehyde is also oxidised to a carboxylic acid.
Apply full oxidation to both the $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ end and the $\text{-CHO}$ end, then join the two resulting $\text{-COOH}$ groups together.
walkthrough:
**Identify the two oxidisable groups**

Think of $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CHO}$ as having a primary alcohol on the left and an aldehyde on the right. Both groups are easily oxidised.

Structure: $$\text{HO-CH}_2\text{-CHO}$$

**Recall strong oxidation conditions**

Excess acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ heated under reflux means vigorous oxidation until no further reaction is possible. This is the strongest outcome, not stopping at the aldehyde stage.

Rules: $$\text{R-CH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{R-CHO} \rightarrow \text{R-COOH}$$
$$\text{R-CHO} \rightarrow \text{R-COOH}$$

**Oxidise each end fully**

The left end $\text{HOCH}_2\text{-}$ is a primary alcohol, so it becomes $\text{HOOC-}$. The right end $\text{-CHO}$ is an aldehyde, so it becomes $\text{-COOH}$.

Result: $$\text{HOCH}_2\text{CHO} \rightarrow \text{HOOC-COOH}$$

**Name the final product**

$\text{HOOC-COOH}$ is ethanedioic acid, with two carboxylic acid groups and still two carbons in total. This matches complete oxidation of both functional groups.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{HOOCCHO}$ shows the alcohol oxidised to acid but the aldehyde left unchanged. Under excess hot dichromate, an aldehyde cannot survive, it must be oxidised to $\text{-COOH}$.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{HOCH}_2\text{COOH}$ shows only the aldehyde oxidised to acid while the primary alcohol is left unchanged. With excess reagent and reflux, the primary alcohol would also be fully oxidised.
options.C: Correct. Both ends are fully oxidised: $\text{HOCH}_2\text{-}$ gives $\text{HOOC-}$ and $\text{-CHO}$ gives $\text{-COOH}$. The product $\text{HOOCCOOH}$ is ethanedioic acid, the result of no further oxidation being possible.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{HOOCCH}_2\text{COOH}$ has three carbons, but the starting material has only two carbons. Oxidation changes functional groups but never adds extra carbon atoms.
